note: Friday pre-Asia-open run, 25 Sep 2026 -- latest completed US session is Thu 24 Sep close: S&P -0.02% to ~7704, Nasdaq +0.01%, Dow -0.31%, Russell2000 -0.11%, VIX +3.2% to ~15.67 (still historically low). The dominant cross-asset driver is a live ~7-month US-Iran war: Iranian threats to widen the conflict plus Houthi missile strikes on Saudi Arabia's Yanbu/Taif sent Brent +3.27% to ~$106.45 and WTI +2.42% to ~$94.39 (IEA calls it the largest oil-supply disruption in market history), while reported US-Iran talks to reopen the Strait of Hormuz capped the spike intraday. Layered on top: the Fed under new Chair Kevin Warsh delivered a hawkish surprise, hiking 25bp to 3.75-4.00% on 16 Sep with more hikes signalled, pushing the 10-year Treasury yield to ~5.0-5.1%, its highest since 2007 -- a firmer dollar drove a gold/silver pullback on 23 Sep that miners (GDX/SILJ/SLVP) extended into Thursday. Sentiment and breadth confirm a narrow, weakening market beneath the still-low VIX: CNN Fear & Greed ticked up slightly to 36/Fear, but under half of S&P names sit above their 200-/50-DMA and the McClellan Oscillator remains deeply oversold. Weekly EPFR/BofA fund-flow data still reflect the pre-war week ended 16 Sep (a cash-into-equities rotation); the next cut, expected in the coming days, should be the first to show any war/Fed-driven reversal.

flows.narrative: The freshest available EPFR/BofA weekly data still cover the week ended 16 September, now nine days stale: global equity funds absorbed a three-month-high +$62.1bn, with US equity funds doing the heavy lifting (+$63.8bn, the largest US weekly haul in 3 months) while Europe funds saw a modest -$0.6bn outflow and Japan (+$1.4bn, 4th straight week) and EM (+$1.4bn, 2nd straight week) extended inflow streaks -- a pronounced US-over-Europe tilt within the broader risk-on move. Money-market funds saw a nine-week-high -$59.5bn redemption funding that rotation; credit was more mixed, with IG inflows slowing to a trickle (+$0.4bn) and HY posting its worst outflow in six months (-$1.9bn), while government bonds/Treasuries kept drawing money (+$2.3bn, a 12-week streak) amid rising rate volatility, and gold ETFs extended a nine-week inflow streak (+$4.24bn) -- separately, monthly World Gold Council-style data point to September being on track for the largest monthly gold-ETF haul on record (~$17bn month-to-date, ~$26bn for Q3), led by North America and Europe. No newer weekly cut has been published as of this research pass; note a minor cross-source rounding gap between the $62.1bn 'global equity' headline and the $63.8bn+$1.4bn+$1.4bn-$0.6bn regional components below (different secondary aggregators of the same underlying BofA/EPFR cut).
